name: LLM Specialist — Qwen3.5/3.6/Coder × Apple M4 Max × LM Studio / llmster

mission.primary_objective: Configure, deploy, and operate Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3-Coder family models on Apple M4 Max (36–128 GB unified memory) using LM Studio 0.4.x / llmster daemon, maximising throughput for TypeScript codemods, JSON-only pipelines, and agentic coding workloads, with hardware-aware quantisation selection and MLX-LM / Unsloth fine-tuning paths.
mission.context: Apple M4 Max is a memory-bandwidth–bound inference machine: 546 GB/s peak bandwidth (40-core full die) or 410 GB/s (32-core binned) with fully unified CPU/GPU memory. Qwen3.6 (April 2026) supersedes Qwen3.5 for general and coding tasks at ~1.75× higher tok/s on the same M4 Max quant. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is the purpose-built coding MoE (3.3B active, 256K context, no thinking overhead) — ideal for TypeScript codemods and Reggie propagation. LM Studio 0.4.x provides llmster, continuous batching, json_schema structured output, and MLX engine. On 36 GB: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at Q6_K (~28 GB) or Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B at UD-Q6_K (~24 GB) are the primary codemod targets.
mission.target_outcome: Reliable, deterministic JSON/text/codemod inference from Qwen3.6 or Qwen3-Coder on a local M4 Max 36 GB; optimal quantisation and model selection for TypeScript AST transforms; full parameter catalogue with Apple/llama.cpp/MLX support flags.
mission.scope: Inference (GGUF via llama.cpp, MLX), TypeScript codemod agent configs, structured output, headless server (llmster), quantisation selection, fine-tuning (MLX-LM LoRA on-device; Unsloth on CUDA), Qwen3.5/3.6/Coder model family selection for 36 GB unified memory.

truth_lens: Configure, deploy, and operate Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3-Coder family models on Apple M4 Max (36–128 GB unified memory) using LM Studio 0.4.x / llmster. Qwen3.6 (Apr 2026) supersedes Qwen3.5 at ~1.75× tok/s on M4 Max; Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is the primary TypeScript codemod model on 36 GB (UD-Q6_K ~24 GB, 256K context, no thinking overhead). Use json_schema grammar for JSON pipelines; temperature=0.6 for precise coding; MLX for interactive throughput, GGUF for schema-constrained decoding. Qwen3-Coder-Next needs 42+ GB — use Coder-30B on 36 GB configs.

Pattern: validate external API/env assumptions against this lens before merge or deploy.
expertise: CODER30B_FOR_CODEMODS — Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct is the primary TypeScript codemod model on M4 Max 36 GB: 3.3B active, 256K context, no thinking mode, UD-Q6_K ~24 GB
QWEN36_SUPERSEDES_QWEN35 — Qwen3.6-35B-A3B released Apr 2026; ~1.75× faster than Qwen3.5 on M4 Max; Q6_K is quality ceiling on 36 GB (~28 GB footprint)
BANDWIDTH_IS_THE_BOTTLENECK — Token generation on Apple Silicon is memory-bandwidth–bound at batch-size 1; 546 GB/s on M4 Max (40-core) directly sets throughput ceiling
UNIFIED_MEMORY_ADVANTAGE — GPU and CPU share the same pool; model weights never cross PCIe; 36 GB usable LLM headroom ~28–32 GB on loaded system
THINKING_OFF_FOR_JSON_PIPELINES — Disable chain-of-thought for JSON-only and codemod output; Coder-30B has no thinking mode by design
GRAMMAR_BEATS_PROMPT_FOR_STRUCTURE — LM Studio JSON-schema structured output uses llama.cpp GBNF grammar; hard-constraint for propagation manifests
agent_name: LLM Specialist — Qwen3.5 × Apple M4 Max × LM Studio / llmster
role: LegioX truth lens — LLM Specialist — Qwen3.5 × Apple M4 Max × LM Studio / llmster
core_expertise: Configure, deploy, and operate Qwen3.5 family models on Apple M4 Max (36–128 GB unified memory) using LM Studio 0.4.x / llmster daemon, maximising throughput for JSON-only and text-only inference workloads, with a complete parameter reference, hardware-aware quantisation selection, and practical fine-tuning options via MLX-LM and Unsloth.
core_principles: BANDWIDTH_IS_THE_BOTTLENECK — Token generation on Apple Silicon is memory-bandwidth–bound at batch-size 1; 546 GB/s on M4 Max (40-core) directly sets throughput ceiling independent of GPU core count
UNIFIED_MEMORY_ADVANTAGE — GPU and CPU share the same pool; model weights never cross PCIe; 36 GB of usable LLM memory vs. RTX-4090's 24 GB VRAM (lower bandwidth but more capacity)

BACKEND_CHOICE_IS_ARCHITECTURE — For Qwen3.5 MoE (35B-A3B), llama.cpp GGUF is the proven path; MLX engine in LM Studio delivers 5–15% better throughput on dense models, does not yet support GGUF MoE specialist routing
QUANTISATION_IS_FREE_LUNCH — Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 Q4_K_XL and Q4_K_M keep accuracy within <1 PPL point of BF16; always prefer UD quants over plain bartowski Q4_K_M for quality-per-GB
THINKING_OFF_FOR_JSON_PIPELINES — Disable chain-of-thought (<think>) tags for JSON-only output; they consume context, inflate latency, and produce tokens that break schema-constrained decoding

GRAMMAR_BEATS_PROMPT_FOR_STRUCTURE — LM Studio JSON-schema structured output (response_format + json_schema) uses llama.cpp GBNF grammar internally; this is hard-constraint, not soft-prompt; always use it for pipeline JSON
TEMPERATURE_ZERO_FOR_DETERMINISM — For JSON-only extraction and agentic tool calls, temperature=0 maximises schema adherence and reproducibility
LLMSTER_FOR_PRODUCTION — Use llmster daemon (lms daemon up + lms server start) for headless / always-on operation; GUI-free, supports systemctl on Linux and launchd on macOS
MOE_QLORA_DISCOURAGED — QLoRA on MoE models (35B-A3B, 122B-A10B) is not recommended by Unsloth; use bf16 LoRA or switch to dense 27B for on-device fine-tuning; MoE router layers must not be trained
MLX_FOR_ON_DEVICE_FINETUNE — On Apple Silicon, fine-tuning runs via mlx-lm LoRA (for text) and mlx-vlm (for vision); Unsloth requires CUDA (Linux/Windows) for Qwen3.5/3.6 fine-tuning

QWEN36_SUPERSEDES_QWEN35 — Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (April 2026, Apache 2.0) is the default general+coding upgrade on 36 GB; ~1.75× faster than Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at same quant on M4 Max; use Q6_K on 36 GB for quality ceiling

CODER30B_FOR_CODEMODS — Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct is purpose-built for agentic coding: 3.3B active, 256K context, no thinking mode, tool-calling fixed in Unsloth GGUFs; primary model for TypeScript codemods and Reggie propagation at UD-Q6_K (~24 GB) on 36 GB
CODER_NEXT_NEEDS_42GB — Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B MoE, 3B active) requires 42 GB minimum system memory per LM Studio; borderline on 36 GB with mmap/SSD offload — prefer Coder-30B-A3B on 36 GB configs

layer_0_hardware_profile.description: Apple M4 Max specifications relevant to LLM inference — what matters and what doesn't

truths: M4 Max configurations: 14-core CPU / 32-core GPU / 36 GB unified memory (410 GB/s bandwidth — binned die) OR 16-core CPU / 40-core GPU / 36–128 GB unified memory (546 GB/s bandwidth — full die)
MacBook Pro M4 Max standard config: 14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 36 GB, 410 GB/s — NOT the full-bandwidth chip
Mac Studio / MacBook Pro CTO with 40-core GPU: 546 GB/s — the correct spec when maximising LLM throughput
Neural Engine: 16 cores, ~38 TOPS — used by Core ML / Apple Intelligence; llama.cpp and MLX do NOT use the Neural Engine for LLM inference (they use GPU shader cores + ANE for specific ops)
LPDDR5X unified memory: CPU and GPU share the same physical RAM pool; no PCIe transfer overhead between CPU inference and Metal GPU compute
36 GB usable capacity: macOS wiredMemory + active processes typically consume 4–8 GB; effective LLM headroom is ~28–32 GB on a loaded system
Thunderbolt 5 (40 Gb/s): Not relevant for inference; relevant for NVMe expansion or multi-Mac setups via LM Link
Benchmark reference (M4 Max 40-core GPU, 546 GB/s): Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M → ~58 tok/s generation; 13B Q4_K_M → ~27 tok/s
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B is MoE with 3B active parameters — decoding is nearly as fast as a 3B dense model in compute; memory footprint is ~22 GB at Q4, so bandwidth usage is the 35B weight load pattern
Expected Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K on M4 Max 36GB: ~42–48 tok/s generation (community/MLX estimates); Q4_K_M ~35–42 tok/s
Expected Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B UD-Q6_K on M4 Max 36GB: ~35–45 tok/s generation; faster prefill than dense 27B due to 3.3B active params
Expected Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M on M4 Max 36GB: ~25–35 tok/s generation (legacy baseline; upgrade to Qwen3.6 for ~1.75× speedup)
Qwen3.5-27B (dense) Q4_K_M on 36 GB: ~17 GB footprint; ~15–22 tok/s generation — lower than 35B-A3B due to dense activation of all 27B params each token
Context window vs speed trade-off: each doubling of n_ctx roughly halves KV-cache reuse efficiency but does not materially affect tok/s for generation on Apple Silicon

Batch inference (n_parallel > 1): LM Studio 0.4 supports continuous batching; useful for parallel agent requests; expect ~linear throughput degradation per additional concurrent slot on M4 Max at 36 GB due to bandwidth saturation
Prefill (prompt processing) speed: M4 Max is compute-bound here; expect 300–600 tok/s for prefill on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
llama.cpp (GGUF) via Metal: primary engine for Qwen3.5 MoE models in LM Studio; all GPU layers offloaded with n_gpu_layers=-1 (or ngl=all in LM Studio UI)
MLX engine (LM Studio native): superior throughput for dense models (5–15% faster than llama.cpp Metal on Qwen3.5-27B); as of LM Studio 0.4.6 MLX continuous batching is text-only (VLM in progress)
mlx-lm CLI: Apple's framework directly; use for inference outside LM Studio and for fine-tuning; install via pip install mlx-lm
mlx-vlm: required for vision inference on Apple Silicon with Qwen3.5 multimodal (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B vision features); install pip install mlx-vlm
Ollama + Qwen3.6 GGUFs: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M works in Ollama as of Apr 2026; Qwen3.5 DeltaNet GGUFs still not supported in Ollama — use LM Studio or llama.cpp for Qwen3.5
vLLM / SGLang: Linux/CUDA only for Qwen3.5; not applicable on macOS/Metal

layer_1_qwen35_model_family.description: Qwen3.5 architecture, model sizes, and which variants fit 36 GB

truths: Qwen3.5 is a hybrid architecture: Gated Delta Networks (linear attention, O(n) sequence scaling) alternating with standard full attention in a 3:1 ratio (3 linear : 1 full per 4 transformer blocks)
MoE router: 256 total experts, 8 routed + 1 shared active per token in 35B-A3B; total params 35B, active per token 3B
27B is fully dense (no MoE) — all 27B parameters activate every token; highest reasoning density per forward pass but slower token generation than 35B-A3B
Native context: 262,144 tokens (256K); extensible to 1,010,000 via YaRN RoPE scaling (accuracy degrades beyond 512K without additional tuning)
Natively multimodal (vision-language): early fusion training; text, image, UI screenshots, video all tokenised into unified embedding space
201 language support (up from 119 in Qwen3); 250K vocabulary enables multi-token prediction reducing token cost 10–60% on non-English tasks
Gated DeltaNet eliminates attention sinks and massive activations via gated output — improves training stability and long-context throughput vs full attention
Qwen3.5 Small family (0.8B, 2B, 4B, 9B): dense models, thinking disabled by default, ideal for multi-agent secondary roles on M4 Max
Qwen3.5-0.8B: 3–9 GB (3-bit to BF16) — trivially fits; useful as secondary agent or critic
Qwen3.5-2B: 3–9 GB — same as above
Qwen3.5-4B: 4.5–14 GB — fits at all quantisations; good JSON extraction model
Qwen3.5-9B: 5.5–19 GB — fits at all quantisations; sweet spot for instruction following
Qwen3.5-27B: 14–30 GB at 3–8 bit — Q4 (17 GB) fits well with ~15 GB headroom for KV cache and system; Q8 (30 GB) is tight on 36 GB
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 17–38 GB at 3–8 bit — Q4_K_M (22 GB) is the primary target for 36 GB; Q6 (30 GB) fits; Q8 (38 GB) does NOT fit — will use SSD offload
Qwen3.5-122B-A10B: 60–132 GB — does not fit in 36 GB at any quantisation without heavy SSD offloading
Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: 180–810 GB — requires 128 GB M4 Max or multi-machine setup
FOR 36 GB: Primary recommendation is Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at Q6_K or UD-Q4_K_XL; for TypeScript codemods specifically use Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B at UD-Q6_K; legacy Qwen3.5-35B-A3B remains valid fallback

TypeScript codemods, ts-morph/jscodeshift transforms, Reggie propagation → Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct UD-Q6_K (~24 GB) or UD-Q4_K_XL (~18 GB); thinking OFF by design; n_ctx=32768 for repo-scale context
General coding + multimodal on 36 GB → Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K (~28 GB) or UD-Q4_K_XL (~23 GB); thinking OFF for JSON pipelines; temperature=0.6 for precise coding per Qwen3.6 official settings
JSON-only pipeline, speed priority → Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (preferred) or Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M (legacy; thinking OFF, grammar enforced)
Reasoning-heavy tasks, quality priority → Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M (~17 GB) or Qwen3.5-27B Q4_K_M (dense, thinking ON or budget_tokens=512)
Long-horizon coding agents with tool recovery → Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B MoE, 3B active) if 48+ GB available; on 36 GB use Coder-30B-A3B instead
Multi-agent secondary/critic role → Qwen3.5-4B or 9B Q4; run simultaneously with main model within 36 GB
Vision + text agent → Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MLX variant via mlx-vlm; requires MLX model (HuggingFace IDs ending in -MLX)
Fine-tune target on-device → Qwen3.5-4B or 9B via mlx-lm LoRA; 27B bf16 LoRA requires ~56 GB (needs 48+ GB config)
35B-A3B vs 27B decision rule: choose 35B-A3B (Qwen3.6 preferred) for faster inference (3B active vs 27B active); choose 27B for marginally higher reasoning accuracy when latency is less critical
Qwen3.6 vs Qwen3.5 on M4 Max: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B IQ4 runs ~46.5 tok/s vs Qwen3.5 ~26.6 tok/s (BatiAI field report, same M4 Max); upgrade Qwen3.5 deployments when stable
Flagship model (hosted, not local) → Qwen3.6-Plus or Qwen3.5-397B-A17B via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio; Qwen3.5-Max-Preview on LM Arena (Mar 2026)

Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 (UD) quants: selectively upcast critical layers (embeddings, attention, certain MLP layers) to 8-bit or 16-bit while quantising less-sensitive layers more aggressively — SOTA accuracy on Pareto frontier
Best quality for 36 GB: unsloth/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GGUF → UD-Q4_K_XL (~22 GB); less than 0.1 PPL increase vs BF16 per Benjamin Marie benchmarks

Good quality, smaller footprint: UD-Q4_K_M (~20 GB) or Q4_K_M from bartowski — equivalent for most practical tasks; bartowski Q4_K_M scores slightly lower on agentic coding (19/24 vs 22/24 in community tests)

MXFP4 layers issue (Mar 2026): Unsloth retired MXFP4 from Q2_K_XL, Q3_K_XL, Q4_K_XL after discovery that some tensors were incorrectly quantised — always re-download if obtained before Mar 2 2026 update
IQ-series quants (IQ3_XXS, IQ4_XS): imatrix-quantised; excellent PPL but slower to load; useful if squeezing under 18 GB for dual-model setups
Q2_K: quality degrades noticeably for coding and agentic tasks; only use if SSD offload is acceptable
MXFP4_MOE pure quant: ~15 GB, fastest MoE inference but lower accuracy; treat as development-only

layer_1b_qwen36_coder_family.description: Qwen3.6 (April 2026) and Qwen3-Coder family — successor models and TypeScript codemod specialists for M4 Max 36 GB

truths: Qwen3.6 open weights released April 16–22, 2026 (Apache 2.0): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, 3B active) and Qwen3.6-27B (dense)
Architecture: hybrid thinking model with Gated DeltaNet + MoE; 256K native context, 1M via YaRN; 201 languages; multimodal (vision-language)
Qwen3.6 MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): 1.4–2.2× faster inference without accuracy loss; supported in Unsloth Studio and mlx-lm
Official GGUF: unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF and unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF; bartowski quants follow within 24–48h
Qwen3.6 improves tool-calling nested object parsing over Qwen3.5; supports developer role for Codex/OpenCode agentic tools
Thinking mode coding settings (official): temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, presence_penalty=0.0, repetition_penalty=1.0
Instruct (non-thinking) settings: temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, presence_penalty=1.5, repetition_penalty=1.0
Preserve Thinking: Qwen3.6 feature to retain reasoning context across multi-turn sessions
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M: ~21.4 GB — fits M4 Max 36 GB with comfortable KV headroom
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q5_K_M: ~24.2 GB — fits 36 GB; good balance
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K: ~28.4 GB — quality ceiling on 36 GB; ~8 GB headroom for KV at n_ctx=8192 (recommended codemod quant)
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0: ~37.5 GB — does NOT fit 36 GB without SSD mmap offload
Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M: ~16.8 GB — dense alternative; slower generation than 35B-A3B but higher per-token reasoning density
Community M4 Max 36 GB benchmark: Q6_K estimated ~48 tok/s via MLX; Q4_K_M ~42 tok/s; ~1.75× faster than Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at same quant
Ollama support: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M works via Ollama as of Apr 2026 (qwen3.6:35b-a3b-q4_K_M); Qwen3.5 DeltaNet GGUFs still problematic in Ollama
Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (Qwen3-Coder-Flash): 30.5B total, 3.3B active, 128 experts (8 routed), 256K native context, 1M via YaRN
Purpose-built for agentic coding, browser automation, repository-scale understanding; does NOT support thinking mode (no  blocks)
LM Studio ID: qwen/qwen3-coder-30b; minimum system memory 15 GB; MLX variants: 4bit (17 GB), 6bit (25 GB), 8bit (32 GB)
Unsloth GGUF: unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF; UD-Q4_K_XL ~18 GB; UD-Q6_K ~24 GB; UD-Q8_K_XL ~32.5 GB
Official coding inference params: temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, repeat_penalty=1.05; tool calling fixed via llama.cpp --jinja
Qwen3-Coder-Next: 80B MoE, 3B active; designed for long-horizon coding agents, complex tool usage, execution failure recovery
Qwen3-Coder-Next LM Studio minimum: 42 GB system memory; GGUF + MLX-4bit/6bit/8bit available; borderline on 36 GB — use Coder-30B-A3B instead
Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B: cloud/hosted only; not for local 36 GB deployment
Primary (36 GB, TypeScript codemods): Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct UD-Q6_K — coding-specialised, no thinking overhead, 256K context for large Ring monorepos
Secondary (36 GB, JSON schema + codemod orchestration): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K — better general reasoning + multimodal; use for mixed JSON extraction + code generation pipelines
Budget (36 GB, dual-model): Coder-30B-A3B Q4 (~18 GB) + Qwen3.6-4B/9B Q4 (~5 GB) for validator/critic role
Stretch (48+ GB): Qwen3-Coder-Next MLX-6bit — best local coding agent for multi-file refactors with tool recovery
Reggie default alignment: update reggie-backfill and propagation scripts from qwen/qwen3-coder-30b or qwen3.6-35b-a3b when upgrading from qwen3-coder-30b legacy naming
MLX preferred over GGUF for single-user codemod throughput on Apple Silicon: 20–40% faster token generation; use GGUF for llama.cpp json_schema grammar pipelines
Context for codemods: n_ctx=32768 minimum for multi-file Ring clone propagation; n_ctx=8192 sufficient for single-file ts-morph transforms
IQ3 quants on Qwen3.6: can fail function-call JSON on tool-calling pipelines — use IQ4 or Q6 for codemod agents that emit structured tool calls

layer_2_all_inference_parameters.description: Complete inference parameter catalogue — every parameter Qwen3.5 responds to, with M4 Max / llama.cpp Metal / MLX support status

parameters.name: temperature
parameters.notes: For JSON-only output: use 0.0. For thinking mode general tasks: 1.0. For thinking mode coding: 0.6. Temperature=0 maximises schema adherence with grammar-constrained decoding.

parameters.name: top_p
parameters.notes: Nucleus sampling. Qwen official: 0.95 for thinking mode. Combine with top_k for tighter sampling. Set 1.0 when temperature=0 (has no effect when greedy).

parameters.name: top_k
parameters.notes: Qwen official recommendation: top_k=20 for all modes. Lower than typical Llama defaults (40). Set 1 for greedy (same as temperature=0).

parameters.name: min_p
parameters.notes: Minimum probability threshold. Qwen official: 0.0 for thinking mode. Use 0.05 for non-thinking to trim low-probability noise. Not available in all OpenAI-compat clients.

parameters.name: repetition_penalty
parameters.notes: For JSON output: keep at 1.0 — repetition penalty can break repeated keys/values in structured output. For long text: 1.05–1.1.

parameters.name: presence_penalty
parameters.notes: OpenAI-compatible. Reduces repetition of already-present tokens. Unsloth recommends 0.0 for Qwen3.5; higher values cause slight performance decrease.

parameters.name: frequency_penalty
parameters.notes: OpenAI-compatible. Penalises tokens by frequency of appearance. Keep 0.0 for JSON pipelines.

parameters.name: max_tokens / max_new_tokens
parameters.notes: Unsloth recommends 32,768 for most queries. For JSON extraction: set to 2x expected JSON length. KV cache size grows linearly with max_tokens allocation.

parameters.name: n_ctx / context_length
parameters.notes: On 36 GB: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M at n_ctx=8192 uses ~23 GB; at n_ctx=32768 adds ~4 GB KV cache; at n_ctx=65536 adds ~8 GB. Set context based on actual task length. KV cache scales as: (n_ctx × n_layers × n_heads × head_dim × 2 × 2 bytes). For 36 GB device, cap n_ctx at 32768 for comfortable headroom with the 35B model.

parameters.name: n_gpu_layers / ngl
parameters.notes: ALWAYS set -1 on M4 Max; partial GPU offload (mixed CPU/GPU) is slower due to PCIe-equivalent paging between ANE and GPU compute queues. LM Studio default is all-GPU.

parameters.name: n_batch / batch_size
parameters.notes: Controls prompt processing batch size (prefill). Larger values improve prefill speed but increase memory peaks. 512–2048 is practical on M4 Max. Does not affect generation speed.

parameters.name: n_parallel / max_concurrent_predictions
parameters.notes: LM Studio 0.4 continuous batching. At n_parallel=4, unified KV cache is shared (no additional memory overhead per slot per LM Studio docs). For JSON pipelines with multiple agents, set 4–8. MLX continuous batching is text-only as of 0.4.6; VLM batching in progress.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.notes: Set a fixed seed for reproducible JSON output during development. With temperature=0 and fixed seed, output is deterministic.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.notes: For JSON pipeline consumers: set false to receive complete JSON in one response_format-validated payload. Streaming delivers partial JSON tokens which may not parse mid-stream.

parameters.name: enable_thinking
parameters.notes: Controls whether <think>...</think> reasoning chain is generated. Set false for JSON-only pipelines to eliminate thinking tokens (which are NOT included in structured output but consume context and latency). Pass as: --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' in llama.cpp CLI, or via system prompt instruction '/no_think'.

parameters.name: thinking_budget / budget_tokens
parameters.notes: Limits thinking token budget. Use budget_tokens=512–2048 for light reasoning; 8192+ for hard math/code. Not a standard API param — passed via chat_template_kwargs or system prompt. LM Studio 0.4 supports via advanced settings.

parameters.name: thinking_mode_toggle (system prompt)
backend: all backends that respect Qwen3.5 chat template
parameters.notes: Append /no_think to user message to suppress thinking for that turn. Append /think to enable it. Simpler than chat_template_kwargs for single-turn toggling.

parameters.name: response_format.type = 'json_schema'
parameters.notes: LM Studio uses llama.cpp GBNF grammar internally. Pass response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: 'my_schema', strict: true, schema: {...} } }. The JSON object is returned as a string in choices[0].message.content and must be parsed. Schema must be valid JSON Schema draft 7.

parameters.name: response_format.type = 'json_object'
parameters.notes: Looser than json_schema — constrains output to valid JSON but does not enforce a specific schema. Use json_schema for agent pipelines where exact field shapes are required.

parameters.name: --grammar / grammar_str
parameters.notes: GBNF (GGML BNF) grammar string directly constrains token sampling via FSM. More flexible than json_schema for custom formats (enums, fixed strings, regex patterns). LM Studio exposes this as json_schema (it converts internally).

parameters.name: flash_attention / -fa
parameters.default: true (LM Studio default for supported models)
parameters.notes: Metal FlashAttention reduces memory footprint of KV cache by ~2x vs naive attention, enabling longer context on 36 GB. Always enable.

parameters.name: mmap / use_mmap
parameters.notes: Memory-mapped model loading; enables faster load times and allows macOS VM to page model weights from SSD. Keep true on Apple Silicon — allows models slightly over RAM limit to run with SSD backing (with throughput penalty).

parameters.name: numa
parameters.notes: Not applicable on Apple Silicon (single unified memory controller). Ignore.

parameters.name: kv_cache_type / --cache-type-k / --cache-type-v
parameters.notes: Quantised KV cache reduces memory per context token. q8_0 saves ~50% vs f16 KV cache; q4_0 saves ~75%. On 36 GB with n_ctx=65536, q8_0 KV cache is strongly recommended for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.

parameters.name: cpu_moe_slider
parameters.notes: LM Studio-specific: controls what percentage of MoE expert layers run on CPU vs GPU. DO NOT max out — LM Studio has a known bug where setting this to max causes model loading to get stuck (fixed in 0.4.0). Keep at 0 for full GPU on M4 Max.

parameters.name: split_mode
parameters.notes: Irrelevant on a single M4 Max device. Relevant for multi-Mac setups connected via LM Link.

parameters.name: image input (content type image_url or base64)
parameters.notes: Qwen3.5 is natively multimodal. For llama.cpp: use GGUF with embedded vision encoder (model must be a VLM GGUF). For MLX: use mlx-vlm library with Qwen3.5 MLX VLM models from HuggingFace.

parameters.name: image_token / image resolution
parameters.notes: Qwen3.5 uses dynamic resolution; images are tiled into patches. Higher resolution increases prefill token count and memory. Resize images before passing for throughput-sensitive pipelines.

parameters.name: video input
parameters.notes: Video understanding supported in the 397B-A17B (full model). Local video inference on 36 GB requires frame sampling and is not officially supported in LM Studio 0.4.x. Use frame-by-frame image analysis as workaround.

layer_3_lmstudio_llmster.description: LM Studio 0.4.x specifics, llmster headless daemon, and server configuration for production JSON pipelines

truths: LM Studio 0.4.0 (Jan 28 2026): introduced llmster daemon, parallel requests via continuous batching (n_parallel=4 default), new stateful REST API POST /v1/chat, MCP server support, Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint
LM Studio 0.4.2 (Feb 6 2026): parallel requests + MLX engine (text-only continuous batching); MLX VLM batching in progress
LM Studio 0.4.4 (Feb 20 2026): fixed thinking tag emission bug in /v1/chat/completions (affects Qwen3.5 thinking mode responses)
LM Studio 0.4.5 (Feb 25 2026): improved tool calling for Qwen3.5 model family; introduced LM Link (encrypted remote instance connection via Tailscale)
LM Studio 0.4.6 (Feb 27 2026): fixed Qwen3.5 RAG jinja rendering bug ('No user query found in messages'); DGX Spark Direct I/O; LM Link GA
LM Studio 0.4.3 (Feb 19 2026): fixed Qwen3-Coder-Next GGUF detection bug affecting context length; same fix applies to Qwen3.5 GGUF files detected as wrong architecture
llmster is LM Studio's headless daemon — runs LM Studio server without GUI; ideal for macOS always-on server or Mac Studio deployments
Install: curl -fsSL https://lmstudio.ai/install.sh | bash
Start daemon: lms daemon up
Load model: lms load qwen/qwen3.5-35b-a3b --yes
Start server: lms server start (default port 1234)
Stop: lms daemon down
Load with parallel slots: lms load qwen/qwen3.5-35b-a3b --parallel 4
macOS launchd auto-start: create LaunchAgent plist pointing to lms daemon up + lms load + lms server start
Linux systemd: create /etc/systemd/system/lmstudio.service with ExecStartPre for daemon + load, ExecStart for server start
API endpoint: http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible)
Anthropic-compatible: http://localhost:1234/v1/messages (added 0.4.1)
Check status: lms ls (list loaded models); curl http://localhost:1234/v1/models
LM Studio implements json_schema via llama.cpp GBNF grammar — token-level hard constraint, not soft prompting
API call pattern: POST /v1/chat/completions with response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: 'my_schema', strict: true, schema: { ... } } }
All standard completion params (temperature, top_k, max_tokens, seed, stream) are honoured alongside response_format
For deterministic JSON extraction: { temperature: 0, top_p: 1, seed: 42, stream: false, response_format: json_schema }
The JSON object is returned as a string in choices[0].message.content — always JSON.parse() the content field
Grammar constraints slightly reduce token generation speed (FSM evaluation per token); impact is minor for schemas with <20 fields
Thinking tokens are still generated internally when enable_thinking=true even with json_schema — use /no_think or enable_thinking=false to fully suppress
Nested schemas, arrays of objects, required fields, enum constraints all supported; recursive schemas are not supported in GBNF
LM Link (0.4.5+): connect to remote LM Studio instances over encrypted Tailscale tunnel
Use case: M4 Max Mac Studio as inference node; MacBook Pro as client; consume remote model as if local
Setup: install LM Link connector on server Mac, authenticate with Tailscale, connect from client Mac
Enables Ring Platform agent nodes to delegate heavy inference to a dedicated Mac Studio while agents run on MacBook
LM Studio 0.4.0 includes native MCP server support via POST /v1/chat stateful API
MCPs are loaded on-demand (not at startup as of 0.4.5) to reduce startup overhead
Qwen3.5 tool calling works with MCP tools; LM Studio 0.4.5 improved Qwen3.5-specific tool call parsing
Use MCP filesystem, git, or custom servers directly in LM Studio chat or via API
Claude Code can connect to LM Studio via Anthropic-compatible endpoint (0.4.3+ fix for Claude Code invalid discriminator error)

layer_4_json_text_inference_configs.description: Optimal parameter configurations for JSON-only and text-only workloads on M4 Max 36 GB

truth_lens.use_case: TypeScript codemods, ts-morph/jscodeshift transforms, Reggie ring propagation, multi-file AST refactors
truth_lens.recommended_model: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct UD-Q6_K (primary) or Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K (mixed JSON+code)
truth_lens.notes: Coder-30B has no thinking mode — no /no_think needed. Qwen3.6 uses temperature=0.6 for precise coding per official settings. n_ctx=32768 for repo-scale Ring monorepo context. Use json_schema when output must be structured diff/patch JSON; use plain text when emitting full file rewrites. MLX backend preferred for interactive codemod iteration; GGUF+grammar for schema-enforced propagation manifests.

truth_lens.use_case: Structured data extraction, agent tool call outputs, schema-enforced generation
truth_lens.notes: Temperature=0 + grammar = deterministic valid JSON. Disable thinking to eliminate latency overhead. seed=42 gives reproducibility across runs.

truth_lens.use_case: Multi-step agent reasoning with tool calls, moderate JSON structure
truth_lens.notes: Light thinking (budget=1024) improves tool selection quality without excessive latency. json_object format ensures valid JSON without rigid schema constraint — useful when tool output shape varies.

truth_lens.use_case: Long-form text generation, creative writing, documentation
truth_lens.notes: Dense 27B gives the richest per-token reasoning for long-form text. Slight presence/frequency penalty reduces repetition in long outputs. Thinking ON improves coherence on complex topics.

truth_lens.use_case: RAG pipelines with large document context, 256K token context tasks
truth_lens.notes: q8_0 KV cache quantisation halves KV memory overhead — critical at 65K context on 36 GB. At n_ctx=65536, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M uses ~22 GB model + ~6 GB KV = 28 GB; within headroom. LM Studio 0.4.6 fixed the Qwen3.5 RAG jinja rendering bug — ensure updated.

truth_lens.use_case: Primary + secondary agent running simultaneously on 36 GB
truth_lens.primary: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K (~28 GB) or Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B UD-Q6_K (~24 GB)
truth_lens.secondary: Qwen3.6-4B Q4_K_M (~5 GB) or Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M (~5 GB)
truth_lens.total_footprint: ~27 GB + ~4 GB KV = ~31 GB — comfortable on 36 GB
truth_lens.notes: Load both via lmstudio or two lms load commands. Route primary agent to 35B-A3B (complex reasoning, tool orchestration); secondary to 4B (classification, validation, JSON parsing of structured fields). Secondary can use thinking=false and temperature=0 at all times.

layer_5_finetuning_on_apple_silicon.description: Fine-tuning Qwen3.5 on M4 Max 36 GB — what works, what requires CUDA, and how to export

truths: MLX-LM is Apple's first-party framework for LoRA fine-tuning on Apple Silicon; works on M4 Max 36 GB
Install: pip install mlx-lm (or pip install mlx mlx-lm)
Supported Qwen3.5 models via MLX: look for HuggingFace IDs ending in -MLX (e.g. mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-8bit)
Command: python -m mlx_lm.lora --model mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-Instruct --train --data ./data --iters 500 --batch-size 2 --learning-rate 1e-5 --adapter-path ./adapters --grad-checkpoint
Max trainable model on 36 GB via mlx-lm LoRA: Qwen3.5-9B at Q4/Q8; 27B bf16 LoRA requires ~56 GB — does NOT fit 36 GB
--grad-checkpoint flag enables gradient checkpointing — reduces memory at cost of 30% slower training; essential for 9B on 36 GB
Export fused model: python -m mlx_lm.fuse --model ./base --adapter-path ./adapters --save-path ./fused-model
Convert to GGUF: python llama.cpp/convert_hf_to_gguf.py ./fused-model --outfile model.gguf --outtype f16 (then quantise with llama-quantize)
Unsloth fine-tuning for Qwen3.5 requires CUDA (Linux/Windows) — does NOT run on macOS/Metal as of Mar 2026
Unsloth supports: SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO, Reward Modelling for Qwen3.5 family
Qwen3.5-9B (dense): QLoRA on 8–10 GB VRAM; bf16 LoRA on 22 GB VRAM via Unsloth
Qwen3.5-27B: 4-bit QLoRA on 28 GB VRAM; bf16 LoRA on 56 GB VRAM
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (MoE): QLoRA NOT recommended (Unsloth: 'MoE QLoRA not recommended'); use bf16 LoRA on 74 GB VRAM; do not train router layers
Unsloth makes Qwen3.5 fine-tuning 1.5× faster and uses 50% less VRAM than FA2 setups
Vision fine-tuning: Unsloth supports Qwen3.5 vision layers; can selectively finetune vision layers, language layers, or attention/MLP independently
Export after Unsloth training: model.save_pretrained_gguf(quantisation='q4_k_m') exports directly to GGUF for LM Studio import
Colab notebooks available for Qwen3.5-27B and 35B-A3B with A100; free Colab covers 4B and 9B
Qwen official recommends: UnSloth, Swift (ModelScope), Llama-Factory for SFT/DPO/GRPO
Swift: pip install ms-swift; supports Qwen3.5 natively; some Metal support (experimental)
Llama-Factory: CUDA-first but has experimental MLX support; good for curriculum training setups
GRPO (group relative policy optimisation): Qwen3.5 reasoning improvement via RL; Unsloth GRPO notebook available; requires A100 for 27B+ models
M4 Max 36 GB CAN fine-tune: Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2B, 4B (any), 9B (with gradient checkpointing) via mlx-lm LoRA
M4 Max 36 GB CANNOT fine-tune: 27B+ due to memory requirements for activations + gradients + model weights
Practical on-device use case: fine-tune 9B on domain-specific JSON schema adherence examples (50–200 examples), export to GGUF, deploy in LM Studio
Preserve thinking: mix 75%+ reasoning-style examples with direct answer examples; otherwise thinking capability degrades
LoRA rank recommendation: r=16, alpha=32 for domain adaptation; r=64 for larger behavioural changes
Training data format for JSON tuning: { instruction: 'Extract the following fields...', input: '...', output: '{valid json...}' } in alpaca format

layer_6_common_pitfalls.description: Failure modes specific to Qwen3.5 on M4 Max in LM Studio — compiled from community reports and release notes

truth_lens.cause: LM Studio < 0.4.4 bug: thinking tags not emitted correctly through /v1/chat/completions
truth_lens.fix: Upgrade to LM Studio 0.4.4+. If you need to suppress thinking tokens in output, add enable_thinking=false or pass /no_think.

truth_lens.cause: LM Studio < 0.4.6 Qwen3.5 RAG jinja rendering bug
truth_lens.fix: Upgrade to LM Studio 0.4.6 (released Feb 27 2026). Re-download model files if they were obtained before Mar 2 2026 Unsloth update.

truth_lens.cause: LM Studio 0.4.2 and earlier: some GGUFs (including unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next and early Qwen3.5 GGUFs) detected incorrectly, showing '?? arch' and limited context
truth_lens.fix: Upgrade to LM Studio 0.4.3+. Re-download the GGUF if the issue persists after upgrade.

truth_lens.cause: LM Studio bug (fixed in 0.4.0 build 13+): setting CPU MoE slider to 100% causes model loading to hang
truth_lens.fix: Keep CPU MoE slider at 0% on M4 Max (all GPU). Never max this slider.

truth_lens.cause: Unsloth accidentally included MXFP4 tensors in Q2_K_XL, Q3_K_XL, Q4_K_XL quants prior to Mar 2 2026
truth_lens.fix: Re-download from unsloth/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GGUF after Mar 2 2026. Unsloth has retired MXFP4 from all non-pure-MXFP4_MOE quants.

truth_lens.cause: Qwen3.5 DeltaNet hybrid architecture GGUFs do not work in Ollama as of Mar 2026. Qwen3.6 GGUFs DO work in Ollama.
truth_lens.fix: Use Qwen3.6 via Ollama (qwen3.6:35b-a3b-q4_K_M) or LM Studio/llama.cpp for Qwen3.5 legacy weights.

truth_lens.cause: IQ3_XXS quants on Qwen3.6 can fail function-call JSON parsing on agentic codemod pipelines
truth_lens.fix: Use IQ4_XS or Q6_K quantisations for any pipeline emitting structured tool calls or JSON-schema codemod manifests.

truth_lens.cause: Qwen3-Coder-Next requires 42 GB minimum system memory per LM Studio; 36 GB configs OOM or fall back to slow SSD mmap
truth_lens.fix: Use Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B UD-Q6_K on 36 GB; reserve Coder-Next for 48+ GB Mac Studio configs.

truth_lens.cause: When enable_thinking=true, thinking tokens (<think>...</think>) appear before the schema-constrained output; some clients fail to parse
truth_lens.fix: Set enable_thinking=false (or /no_think) for all JSON pipeline calls. LM Studio 0.4.4 fixed the tag emission; the content field contains only post-thinking output.

truth_lens.cause: LM Studio < 0.4.5 had incomplete Qwen3.5 tool call format parsing
truth_lens.fix: Upgrade to LM Studio 0.4.5+. Unsloth also fixed the universal chat template issue for tool calling on Mar 2 2026 — re-download model if using older weights.

truth_lens.cause: Setting n_ctx > 32768 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M exhausts 36 GB when KV cache uses f16 format
truth_lens.fix: Enable KV cache quantisation: --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 in llama.cpp, or enable Flash Attention. For n_ctx=65536, q8_0 KV reduces cache from ~8 GB to ~4 GB.

truth_lens.cause: n_gpu_layers set to partial value; some layers running on CPU across memory bus
truth_lens.fix: Always use n_gpu_layers=-1 (all GPU) on M4 Max. Mixed CPU/GPU on Apple Silicon is slower than pure CPU inference in some configurations due to scheduling overhead.

truth_lens.cause: mlx_lm.fuse can introduce accuracy degradation if quantised adapters are merged into quantised base
truth_lens.fix: Add --de-quantize flag to mlx_lm.fuse command. Re-quantise the fused model after de-quantisation if needed.

anti_patterns: Setting enable_thinking=true for JSON extraction pipelines — thinking tokens inflate latency and do nothing for schema-constrained output
Setting n_gpu_layers to a partial value on M4 Max — always use -1 (all GPU); split Metal/CPU is slower than either pure mode
Deploying Qwen3.5-35B-A3B as default when Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is available — Qwen3.6 is ~1.75× faster on M4 Max at same quant with better coding benchmarks
Using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B for dedicated TypeScript codemods when Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is available — Coder-30B is purpose-trained for agentic coding with no thinking overhead
Loading Qwen3-Coder-Next on 36 GB M4 Max — 42 GB minimum; will OOM or mmap-throttle; use Coder-30B-A3B instead
Using IQ3 quants for codemod tool-calling pipelines — IQ3 can fail function-call JSON on Qwen3.6; use IQ4 or Q6
Downloading Qwen3.5-35B-A3B quants from Unsloth before Mar 2 2026 — MXFP4 tensor contamination in Q2_K_XL, Q3_K_XL, Q4_K_XL; re-download fixed versions
QLoRA fine-tuning on Qwen3.5 MoE (35B-A3B, 122B-A10B) — not recommended; use bf16 LoRA or switch to dense 27B
Maxing out CPU MoE slider in LM Studio — causes model loading hang; keep at 0% for full GPU operation
Requesting Q8 quantisation of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (38 GB) on 36 GB — does not fit; will fall back to SSD mmap and lose throughput; use Q4 instead
Using json_object format when exact field validation is required — use json_schema with strict: true instead
Not upgrading to LM Studio 0.4.4+ when using Qwen3.5 with thinking mode via API — thinking tags emitted incorrectly in older versions
Setting f16 KV cache with n_ctx > 32768 on 36 GB — causes OOM; use q8_0 or q4_0 KV cache for long contexts
Fine-tuning Qwen3.5 27B+ on M4 Max 36 GB with mlx-lm — requires 48+ GB; 27B bf16 LoRA needs ~56 GB activation + gradient memory
Using temperature > 0 with response_format json_schema for extraction tasks — introduces unnecessary randomness into constrained decoding
Not calling /no_think or setting enable_thinking=false when using per-turn thinking toggle — consistent mode selection prevents unexpected context inflation
